[CHAPTER 246.] JOINT RESOLUTION
To extend until April 1, 1936, certain provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and for other purposes.
Resolved by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United 
States of America in Congress assembled, That section 2 (c) of Title I 
of the National Industrial Recovery Act is amended by striking out 
“ at the expiration of two years after the date of enactment of this 
Act ” and inserting in lieu thereof “ on April 1, 1936 ”.
Sec . 2. All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power 
to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and 
providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed: 
Provided, That the exemption provided in section 5 of such title 
shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder (1) putting 
into effect the requirements of section 7 (a), including minimum 
wages, maximum hours, and prohibition of child labor; and (2) pro-
hibiting unfair competitive practices which offend against existing 
law, including the antitrust laws, or which constitute unfair methods 
of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, as 
amended.
Approved, June 14, 1935.

Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed", so the prospective operative effect of this approval ended on June 14, 1935, the date of approval, because the resolution states no later effective date. The held later amendments extended the code's expiration date from December 31, 1933 to June 16, 1935 and none ended the code earlier. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended earlier, and the order states no own-terms end. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. The Schechter decision of May 27, 1935 is recorded only as a validity characterization, not an end date.

To extend until April 1, 1936, certain provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and for other purposes.
Resolved by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United 
States of America in Congress assembled, That section 2 (c) of Title I 
of the National Industrial Recovery Act is amended by striking out 
“ at the expiration of two years after the date of enactment of this 
Act ” and inserting in lieu thereof “ on April 1, 1936 ”.

to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and 
providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed:

wages, maximum hours, and prohibition of child labor; and (2) pro-

law, including the antitrust laws, or which constitute unfair methods 
of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, as 
amended.

A Code of Fair Competition for the Artificial Flower and Feather Industry has been heretofore approved by me. After such approval, and in accordance with the provisions of my further Executive order dated July 15, 1933, hearings have been granted by the Administrator to the named applicants, allegedly directly affected by said code, who have claimed that applications thereof have been unjust to them and have applied for an exemption therefrom.

Roosevelt, President of the United States, pursuant to the authority and discretion vested in me under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, and in accordance with the provisions of my Executive order dated July 15, 1933, providing for hearing on the application of codes under certain circumstances, do order that the application for exemption by the above-named applicants be and it is hereby denied.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT,

President.

November 4, 1933.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The proviso commands that "the provisions of Section 24 of Article VII shall not become effective, and they are hereby stayed for a period of twenty days in order to afford consideration to the objections of any interested parties, and that at the expiration of such period the provisions of such section shall become effective, unless I shall otherwise order". The stay is an own-terms fixed period: the order is dated June 30, 1934 and stays Section 24 of Article VII for "a period of twenty days", so the stay expired on July 20, 1934, twenty days after the order's date, and at the expiration of such period the section "shall become effective". The recorded date is July 20, 1934; if the day of the order is counted as the first day, the last day of the stay is July 19, 1934, and the section becomes effective the next day. The stay reserves the President's power to order otherwise, and no held order exercises it, so the stay ended before June 14, 1935 and the repeal of June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 section 2) is a later event as to this clause.

[CHAPTER 246.] JOINT RESOLUTION
To extend until April 1, 1936, certain provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and for other purposes.
Resolved by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United 
States of America in Congress assembled, That section 2 (c) of Title I 
of the National Industrial Recovery Act is amended by striking out 
“ at the expiration of two years after the date of enactment of this 
Act ” and inserting in lieu thereof “ on April 1, 1936 ”.
Sec . 2. All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power 
to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and 
providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed: 
Provided, That the exemption provided in section 5 of such title 
shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder (1) putting 
into effect the requirements of section 7 (a), including minimum 
wages, maximum hours, and prohibition of child labor; and (2) pro-
hibiting unfair competitive practices which offend against existing 
law, including the antitrust laws, or which constitute unfair methods 
of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, as 
amended.
Approved, June 14, 1935.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order commands "I hereby approve said amendment and modify my previous approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Industry to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended" under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act for the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverage Wholesale Industry; the approval has legal effect only through section 3 of that title (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed", so the prospective operative effect of this approval ended on June 14, 1935, the date of approval, because the resolution states no later effective date. The command approves amendments whose text is not in the order and modifies the previous approval so that it covers the code as amended; it depends on section 3 in the same way as the original approval. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended earlier, and the order states no own-terms end. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. The Schechter decision of May 27, 1935 is recorded only as a validity characterization, not an end date.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

To summarize and conclude upon this point: Section 3 
of the Recovery Act is without precedent. It supplies no 
standards for any trade, industry or activity. It does not 
undertake to prescribe rules of conduct to be applied to 
particular states of fact determined by appropriate admin-
istrative procedure. Instead of prescribing rules of con-
duct, it authorizes the making of codes to prescribe them.

tation, correction and expansion described in section one.

research_rationale:
The held American Presidency Project transcription of EO:7016 (signed April 19, 1935) recites that the Federal Alcohol Control Administration submitted amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverages Importing Industry with its report, and that notice and a hearing were given, then commands "I hereby approve said amendments and modify my previous approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Alcoholic Beverages Importing Industry to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended". The text of the amendments is not in the order. It states no period, condition, "until" date, exception or provisional approval, so no own-terms end applies. The command depends wholly on section 3 of Title I (approval of a code as amended), and under the reviewed shared analysis its first end is the statutory repeal on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 section 2, "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; approved June 14, 1935) unless a held record shows an earlier cancellation or suspension, and none is held.

[CHAPTER 246.] JOINT RESOLUTION
To extend until April 1, 1936, certain provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and for other purposes.
Resolved by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United 
States of America in Congress assembled, That section 2 (c) of Title I 
of the National Industrial Recovery Act is amended by striking out 
“ at the expiration of two years after the date of enactment of this 
Act ” and inserting in lieu thereof “ on April 1, 1936 ”.
Sec . 2. All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power 
to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and 
providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed: 
Provided, That the exemption provided in section 5 of such title 
shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder (1) putting 
into effect the requirements of section 7 (a), including minimum 
wages, maximum hours, and prohibition of child labor; and (2) pro-
hibiting unfair competitive practices which offend against existing 
law, including the antitrust laws, or which constitute unfair methods 
of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act, as 
amended.
Approved, June 14, 1935.
